newsitem.title: GERMANY: Slot losses feared by European regional airlines.
newsitem.headline: Slot losses feared by European regional airlines.

text.p: Regional airlines face the possible loss of airport slots, additional costs and increased passenger liability under proposed European Union transport rules, a senior European Regional Airlines association (ERA) executive said on Friday.

Andrew Clarke, ERA assistant director air transport policy, told the association's annual meeting that European Commission proposals on airports slots expected within the next few weeks could put regional airlines at risk by reviewing current International Air Transport Association (IATA) regulations.
"There is a small risk that the routes and rights or regional airlines will be jeopardised," he added.

Separately ERA director general Mike Ambrose told a news conference that:"Liberalisation has worked, we have passenger growth and now we have a shortage of slots. The European Commission is looking for new slot ideas because they cannot insist of more airport capacity."
The commission could not seek to take slots away from existing carriers, including smaller airlines, to meet the demands of larger European carriers, he warned.
Ambrose said the ERA would also lobby to reverse the European Union decision to end duty-free sales in July 1999 since this would cause a substantial loss of income for airports.
The effect could be to force airports to raise aircraft charges to replace the lost revenue, which would lead to higher passenger prices, or to reduce infrastructure improvements, he said.

Clarke added planned European Union regulations on passenger liability might force airlines to make rapid payments of large sums of money to alleged accident victims which could not be reclaimed in cases of fraud or mistaken identity.

He called on Brussels to allow airlines to self-regulate through an IATA inter-carrier agreement instead of imposing restrictions on the industry. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
